body: Is this a bug, though? The error message is "Opening curly brace does not appear on the same line as the block identifier.", which is true.

By the way, if we just want the rule to make sure there's no line terminator between the `)` and `{`, that should be a really easy fix. Just use `context.getTokens(block, 1)` and make sure the first and second token are on the same line.

On one hand, you are correct, based on the text of the message, everything is fine. However, documentation for this rule is talking about one true brace style, and having multiple arguments is not against one true brace style, so the rule should probably honor this case.
Any thoughts on what a better error message might say? I've got some writers block on this.
"Opening curly brace does not appear on the same line as the block identifier condition."?
@iancmyers: there's some issues with the approach you've taken. In short, blocks can appear in other places. I'm going to work on an alternative commit.
